challenges.name: agent-change-scope-quiz
challenges.title: Did the agent stay in scope?
challenges.description: Two diffs from agent PRs on the catalog: one with a rename the first scope check missed, one with a file the allowed glob does not cover.

questions.question:
Task: "Fix the level filter on the catalog page". Allowed paths: src/catalog/**, tests/catalog/**.

$ git diff --name-status main...agent/catalog-level
M	src/catalog/filterCourses.ts
A	tests/catalog/filterCourses.test.ts
R100	db/migrations/20261003_add_course_level.sql	src/catalog/legacy/20261003_add_course_level.sql

The first version of the scope check looked only at the new path of each change and printed:
scope: ok (3 changes, all inside allowed paths)

Statement: "The check is right: every file this diff touches ends up under src/catalog or tests/catalog, so the migrations folder is unchanged."
questions.explanation: False. R100 means the file was moved without edits, and a move changes two paths: it adds src/catalog/legacy/20261003_add_course_level.sql and removes db/migrations/20261003_add_course_level.sql. The migration runner reads db/migrations, so on the next fresh database (a new developer, CI, a preview environment) the level column is never created. A scope check must check both the old and the new path of a rename, and deletions too: removing a file is a change to that path. The misconception is that a rename is a change to the destination only.

questions.question:
Task: "Add a level filter helper". Allowed paths in the task file: src/catalog/*.ts, tests/catalog/*.test.ts.

$ git diff --name-status main...agent/level-helper
M	src/catalog/filterCourses.ts
A	src/catalog/filters/byLevel.ts
A	tests/catalog/filters/byLevel.test.ts

The harness uses the glob rules of this lesson: "*" matches characters inside one path segment, "**" matches whole segments.

Statement: "The scope check reports src/catalog/filters/byLevel.ts and tests/catalog/filters/byLevel.test.ts as outside the allowed paths."
questions.explanation: True. In src/catalog/*.ts the * can only match characters inside one segment, so it matches src/catalog/filterCourses.ts but not src/catalog/filters/byLevel.ts, whose name sits one folder deeper; the same holds for the test. The agent did nothing dangerous here - it created a sub-folder - which is exactly why the check is useful: either the task's scope was too narrow (write src/catalog/**/*.ts) or the agent restructured more than it was asked to, and a person decides which. The misconception is that * means "everything below this folder".

challenges.name: agent-change-scope-check
challenges.title: Check the agent's diff against its allowed paths
challenges.description:
After the coding agent finishes a task, the CodeDev harness compares the changed files with the paths the task allows and the paths no task may touch (migrations, CI config, lockfiles unless the task allows them, secrets), and refuses to open the PR while there are violations. Write matchGlob(pattern, path) and checkScope(changes, allowed, forbidden).

Paths to check: added, modified and deleted changes give their path; a renamed change gives two, its old path (from) as change "renamed-from" and its new path (path) as "renamed-to". For each path the first of these that applies is a violation, otherwise the path is fine: (1) "invalid path": empty, contains "\", or has a segment (between "/") that is empty, "." or ".." (so a leading or trailing "/" is invalid); (2) "forbidden: <pattern>": the first entry of forbidden, in list order, whose pattern matches - skipping an entry with unlessAllowed true when the path matches an allowed pattern; (3) "outside allowed paths": no allowed pattern matches.

Return { ok, checked, violations }: checked = number of paths checked, ok = no violations, violations = [{ path, change, reason }] sorted by path, then by change (strings compared with < and >).

matchGlob matches the whole path. Braces first: "{" starts a group that ends at the next "}"; the text between is split on "," and one alternative must match; several groups give every combination; an alternative may be empty; a "{" with no "}" after it is a plain character. Then pattern and path are split on "/". A segment that is exactly "**" matches zero or more whole path segments. In other segments "*" matches any run of characters (also none) and "?" exactly one, both inside that segment only, and they also match a leading "."; every other character matches itself, case-sensitive (".", "(", ")", "[", "]", "+" are plain). So "*.pem" does not match "certs/dev.pem" and "**/*.pem" does.

Input: { allowed, forbidden: [{ pattern, unlessAllowed }], changes: [{ status: "added" | "modified" | "deleted", path } | { status: "renamed", from, path }] }. The test runner prints the report as JSON.
hints: When a file is renamed, which paths did the change touch: only where the file is now, or also where it was? And when a path matches both an allowed and a forbidden pattern, which one wins - does it depend on the forbidden entry?

Split the work. Expand the braces into a list of plain patterns. Compare a pattern with a path segment by segment, letting a "**" segment take zero, one or more path segments (a small recursive function over two indexes does it). Inside one segment translate * and ? and escape every other character if you build a regular expression - ( [ . + mean something to RegExp. Then check each path in the order invalid, forbidden, allowed, and sort at the end with a comparator on path, then change.

A worked example with another pattern: docs/**/{intro,faq}.md expands to docs/**/intro.md and docs/**/faq.md. Against docs/faq.md: docs = docs, ** takes zero segments, faq.md = faq.md, so it matches. Against docs/v2/guides/intro.md: ** takes v2 and guides, it matches. Against docs/intro.mdx: intro.md is not intro.mdx, no match. And docs/*.md against docs/v2/intro.md: one * cannot take v2/intro, no match.

tests.name: The incident PR: CI config, lockfile and a rename outside the task
Glob basics: * stays in one segment, ** spans zero or more, ? and {a,b}
Renames count for both paths; deleted files are checked; ties sort by change
Lockfiles only when the task allows them; secrets and keys never
Special characters are literal: route groups, [slug], dots
Invalid paths are violations, also as the old path of a rename
An empty diff is in scope
Large PR: 1,004 changes across the repository
